subject: Using data from dynamic renderUI input

messages.author: fa8b9dad524607ca
messages.subject: Using data from dynamic renderUI input
parts:
Hello,

First, let me start by saying that shiny is awesome.  When I first saw it displayed at a recent bioconductor workshop I was blown away with the sleek design and the potential range of applications.  In the past, I had made an R script which interacted with user input, but it was very limited, generalized and primitive relative to shiny.  Now, I am trying to explore the extent to which it can be applied to an upcoming project, which will require a good amount of user input to determine which data should be used and which established R functions should be run, and then later playing with the results to essentially get it to 'look nice'.

Currently, I have created a test "Frankenstein" program, made from chopped up bits from the tutorial and implementing renderUI, to try to accomplish the following:
Select the 'column of interest'
Select 'elements of interest' from within 'the column of interest'
Be able to use the 'elements of interest' in some way

I have accomplished the first two miniature goals, but the third eludes me.  I am unable to figure out how to have the 'checked' elements be used further.  Any input would be greatly appreciated.  Below is my code:

-----ui.R-----
library(shiny)
library(datasets)

playerChoices <- colnames(mtcars) #simulate the annotation file
names(playerChoices) <-colnames(mtcars) #simulate the annotation file

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(


  headerPanel("Miles Per Gallon"),


  sidebarPanel(
    selectInput("variable", "Variable:",
                playerChoices), #make the choices of the drop down box equal to the columns of the simulated annotion file

   
    uiOutput("cityControls") #generate the myriad of check boxes
  ),


  mainPanel(
    h3(textOutput("caption")),

    plotOutput("mpgPlot"), #check to make sure the selection from the drop down is functional
    h3(textOutput("citiestext")) #either text or plotOutput, just want to play with it somehow
  )
))



----server.R----
library(shiny)
library(datasets)


mpgData <- mtcars
mpgData$am <- factor(mpgData$am, labels = c("Automatic", "Manual"))


shinyServer(function(input, output) {


  formulaText <- reactive({
    paste("mpg ~", input$variable)
  })
 citiesx <-    reactive({
 class(input$cities) #what is input$cities, how can it be used?
 })
 

  output$caption <- renderText({
    formulaText()
  })


  output$mpgPlot <- renderPlot({
    boxplot(as.formula(formulaText()), #boxplot whichever comparison is made
            data = mpgData            )#,
            #outline = input$outliers)
  })
 
  output$cityControls <- renderUI({
  cit <-    unique(mpgData[,input$variable]) #find the numbers inside the column selected

 
  checkboxGroupInput("cities", "Choose Numbers", cit) #make them into checkboxes ... how do I use them?
})

  output$citiestext <- renderText({
    paste(citiesx) #was hoping to get a look at it somehow, either with rendexText or Plot?

  })
})

----back to talking----

Thank you for your time and attention,
Mike

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Using data from dynamic renderUI input
parts:
Thanks for the kind words!

In your example, input$cities is a character vector of the selected values. You could have put input$cities directly in the renderText at the end rather than wrapping it in citiesx; although citiesx would have worked as well IF in the renderText part you did "citiesx()" instead of "citiesx". (To read a reactive expression, you call it like a function.)

Next time you want to see what different variables look like, just put a browser() call in the middle of i.e. the renderText call there, and call runApp(). From the browse prompt you can just enter input$cities or whatever.

In the future we hope to make this particular scenario (using input A to populate input B) easier to accomplish without using reactiveUI at all.

-joe

Dear Joe,
Thanks for your reply on this group. I am new to Shiny, but I have been trying create a small app that displays a unique interface based on the user's choice. On a page, there will be radio buttons which allows a user to display an interface per time. Please look at my codes below:

-- ui.R

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar( ## I would prefer a page without a side bar, don't know which to specify, my radio buttons won't display properly except I use this page with side bar

  headerPanel("My Title"),

  sidebarPanel(), # I don't know how to create a page that would allow my radio buttons display properly, that's why I left this blank

  mainPanel(
    radioButtons("option", h5("Select Calculation Type:"),
                 c("Calculation 1" = "option1",
                   "Calculation 2" = "option2"
                   )
                 ),
    uiOutput("outputId")
  )
  
))

-- server.R

shinyServer(function(input,output){
  calc1 <- reactive({           # This is one option of the interface
    input1 <- numericInput("Pwf", "Pressure:", 5650)
    input2 <- numericInput("intv", " Intervals:", 200)
    input3 <- dataTableOutput("view")
    input4 <- plotOutput("miplot")
    list(input1,input2,input3,input4)
  })
  
  calc2 <- reactive({        # This is the other option
    input1 <- checkboxInput("cPrx", "Productivity:", FALSE)
    input2 <- numericInput("Prx", "Index:", 1.2)
    input3 <- numericInput("Pwf", "Pressure:", 5650)
    input4 <- fileInput("file", 
                        accept=c("text/csv","text/comma-separated-values, text/plain"),
                        ".csv",h6("Select file (csv only"))
    input5 <- dataTableOutput("view1")
    list(input1,input2,input3,input4,input5)
  })
  
  testFunction <- reactive({
    option1 <- calc1()
    option2 <- calc2()
    
    switch(input$option,
           "option1" = option1,
           "option2" = option2
           )
    
  })
  
  output$outputId <- renderUI({
    testFunction()
  })
  
})

When I try to run the app, the radio buttons display but and there is an error "Error: argument is not interpretable as logical". I'll be obliged if you'd be willing to help understand what I'm doing wrongly.
Thank you.

Tunde
